arguments.summary: Conditional company contribution: the supplied grids anchor FY2027 NVDA and FY2026 MU to reported interim GAAP EPS and management outlook, but use explicitly hypothetical annual EPS/P/E inputs. They demonstrate materially different earnings bridges and direct-issuer sensitivities; they do not establish fair value, probability, or a whole-team preference versus QQQ.

claims.text: NVDA’s FY2027 is a disclosed 53-week year ending 2027-01-31. Reported first-half GAAP diluted EPS was $4.85 through 2026-07-26; the $9.50 base assumption therefore requires $4.65 for the remaining 27 weeks under a constant split-adjusted-share approximation. This is conditional on Q3 revenue being near management’s $108bn ±2% outlook and on a profitable un-guided Q4. The disclosed Q3 outlook assumes no China Data Center compute revenue, while the reported Q2 Data Center result and platform ramp support AI-infrastructure demand as the operating driver. A demand/order normalization, supply disruption, China constraint, or margin compression would instead support the $3.65 bear residual; continuing execution through Q4 supports the $5.65 bull residual. Residuals are not exact annual reconciliations because actual diluted shares may change.

At the 2026-09-18 split-adjusted close, NVDA’s hypothetical $8.50×18, $9.50×24, and $10.50×30 cases produce -31.16%, +2.58%, and +41.72% sensitivities. In the base, the close equates to $9.26125 EPS holding 24x, or 23.3968x holding $9.50 EPS; exceeding either threshold, with the other input held fixed, is required for upside. Bull gain exceeds bear-loss magnitude by 10.55 percentage points, but that asymmetry supplies no probability or fair-value conclusion. Evidence reversing this conditional bridge would be Q3 results materially outside revenue/margin outlook or Q4 demand/margin evidence that changes the residual-EPS assumption.

MU’s FY2026 is a disclosed 53-week year ending 2026-09-03, with a 14-week fourth quarter. Reported GAAP diluted EPS was $41.40 for the first 39 weeks through 2026-05-28. The $72 base case requires a $30.60 residual under a constant split-adjusted-share approximation, near management’s Q4 GAAP EPS outlook of $30.73 ±$1.00. AI-memory demand, pricing, and high margins are the stated operating bridge; weaker memory pricing/volume or margin supports the $28.60 bear residual below guidance, while stronger demand/pricing and execution supports the $32.60 bull residual above guidance. The actual Q4 result was scheduled for September 30, so the ended FY remains a provisional historical estimate in this analysis, not next-year EPS.

At the 2026-09-18 split-adjusted close, MU’s hypothetical $70×12, $72×15, and $74×18 cases produce -17.31%, +6.32%, and +31.13% sensitivities. The base close equates to $67.72 EPS holding 15x, or 14.1083x holding $72 EPS; surpassing a threshold with the other input fixed is needed for upside. Bull gain exceeds bear-loss magnitude by 13.82 percentage points, without probability or fair-value inference. The September 30 report—especially Q4 EPS, memory pricing/volume and margin evidence—would directly revise the residual-EPS bridge.

QQQ’s dated 2026-09-18 equity holdings included NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%, within 99.859505% reported equity-weight coverage; its sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08 as of 2026-08-31. Thus QQQ includes both company drivers but is not equivalent to direct single-issuer exposure. The issuer grids’ assumed 18–30x and 12–18x P/Es cannot be ranked against the sponsor aggregate P/E without matching methodology, forecasts, and weights.

gaps.description: No consensus, observed issuer P/E, empirical multiple history, or verified forward diluted-share forecast is supplied. The stress grids remain valid as explicitly hypothetical sensitivities, but no fair/normal multiple, probability, or unconditional cross-company valuation ranking is supported.

QQQ holdings are dated sponsor weights and omit/qualify cash, derivatives and an unknown-weight position; QQQ’s aggregate P/E has a different fund methodology. This supports overlap identification, not a quantified current portfolio exposure or issuer-to-fund valuation equivalence.

The supplied policy excerpts identify possible export/trade and supply channels but do not quantify issuer exposure or certify the current regime. This role does not quantify policy impact on annual EPS.

assumptions: NVDA grid: FY2027 GAAP EPS of $8.50/$9.50/$10.50 and P/E of 18x/24x/30x are stress inputs; reported interim EPS is combined only through a constant split-adjusted-share approximation.
MU grid: FY2026 GAAP EPS of $70/$72/$74 and P/E of 12x/15x/18x are stress inputs; reported interim EPS is combined only through a constant split-adjusted-share approximation.
Scenario period lengths differ from the 63-session research horizon; scenario prices are sensitivities, not price targets or forecasts.
arguments.counter_thesis: The recent reported demand and guidance could prove more durable than the bear bridges assume, while a stable-or-higher multiple could amplify gains. Conversely, neither reported growth nor the scenario asymmetry demonstrates that either assumed multiple will persist; normalization or multiple compression can occur even if EPS meets the base case.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA after the next reported results: revise the remaining-FY EPS bridge if Q3 revenue/margin differs materially from the disclosed $108bn ±2% revenue and 74.0% ±50bp GAAP gross-margin outlook, or if Q4 demand evidence alters the $4.65 base residual assumption.

Review MU after the scheduled September 30 FY2026 Q4 report: replace the provisional $30.60 base residual with reported EPS and reassess memory pricing, volume and margin against the $30.73 ±$1.00 GAAP outlook.

Review QQQ overlap if sponsor holdings update materially: changed NVDA/MU weights or reported coverage would alter the direct-versus-fund look-through comparison, but not retroactively establish current weights.

shared_exposures.mechanism: QQQ’s dated holdings embed both NVDA and MU, so AI-infrastructure demand or semiconductor-cycle shocks can affect direct positions and the fund through those constituents.
shared_exposures.qualification: This is dated constituent overlap only; it does not quantify total semiconductor exposure, fund returns, or an investor allocation.
